records.choice: The v2 script, verbatim (files/short-eo04-song-remembers-script-v2.md): de-signed (no 'Say it plainly'), 'almost unchanged' scoped to depended-on songs on the Rigveda/songline record, bridge written fresh, temporal opener KEPT deliberately (Ep.3's was the one rewritten — the split is logged in both docs).
records.alternatives: The v1 draft — superseded by its logged weak points (unscoped fidelity claim, stock bridge, twin opener).
records.context: Phase 1 Narrative Gate + retention Decision Records (DR-E4-CLICK / DR-E4-CONTINUE) inside the script doc; structure beat-sheet lite; villain = words without a beat; N-09 statement at L7, unannounced.
records.why: The script doc IS this section of the record.
records.change: A canon ruling or a retention signal against a specific line reopens that line's block in the script doc.

records.element: Scene plate — the grandmother singing the road (L1–L2, L7 + opening card)
records.choice: Generated plate (second take): grey-bunned grandmother in a rust tunic leading two tunic-clad, barefoot children along the path, all singing; the big rock and the bent tree stand on the path behind them. First take REJECTED at inspection: its children wore modern clothes and shoes — an anachronism against the locked world anchors; the rejection and its reason are part of this record.
records.alternatives: The first take (rejected, above); the empty road for L1 (rejected — the script's DR-E4-CONTINUE: the grandmother must exist before words can fail her).
records.context: Format v4 world anchors; V-06 inspect-before-use; K-02 series consistency.
records.why: The episode's one concrete example (T-17) is this woman and this road; both verses' landmarks are visible in her first frame.
records.change: If Studio retention dips at 0–5 s, the opening image is the first suspect.

records.element: Scene plate — the empty road (L4, L5 second half, L6)
records.choice: Generated plate: the winding path, the big rock, the bent tree, a very large pale sky — no people, on purpose: this is the stage the notes component travels.
records.alternatives: Cropping the grandmother plate — rejected: the road must be empty for the notes' arrangements (line, trail) to read as events, not decorations.
records.context: H-01: the plate is the canvas; the notes are separate components over it.
records.why: L4's claim (a beat holds words in line) and L6's (the song travels) are performed by components ON this emptiness.

records.element: Scene plate — words without a beat (L3)
records.choice: Generated plate: three rust-tunic figures at dusk on the dimmed plain, one scratching his head, an unlit fire laid beside them. The notes component is ABSENT for this entire beat — the absence is designed, not an omission.
records.alternatives: Showing scattered/falling notes — rejected: a wrong-note gag would make the failure cute; the script's failure is silent drift, and an empty sky over puzzled faces states it colder.
records.context: N-06: the villain gets a beat with no rescue in it; S-05 one signal at a time.
records.why: When the notes return in a line at L4, the viewer feels the difference the beat makes — because they just sat in its absence.
records.change: If frame QC finds L3 reading as a rendering gap rather than a designed absence, a single faint fallen note is added at the fire's edge — and this record is amended, not silently edited.

records.element: Scene plate — Ep.1's waterhole (L5 first 55%, reused) + mid-line cut to the road
records.choice: Ep.1's own waterhole frame for 'where the water is,' cutting mid-line (55%) to the empty road for 'which plants heal, which plants kill' — the Ep.2 L7 mid-line cut pattern.
records.alternatives: Staying on the grandmother plate for all of L5 — rejected: L5 is a cargo list, and the series' rule (Ep.2 precedent) is that a change of subject inside a line earns a cut.
records.context: Series Chekhov: the water road is Ep.1's world; V-03 every scene illustrates the exact words over it.
records.why: The viewer sees the water the song exists to find, inside the line that names it.
records.change: If Ep.1's frame is ever rebuilt, this plate follows it.

records.element: Scene plate — the child tracing in sand (L9)
records.choice: Generated plate: a blank-oval child kneeling, tracing curves in smooth sand, while the grandmother — here with a warm, faced, laughing rendering — sings beside her under a morning sun.
records.alternatives: The grandmother plate + an 'A B C' label alone — kept as the label's job anyway (the label IS present); rejected as the whole visual: L9's twist is a person, not a caption.
records.context: N-08 bookend twist: prehistory → the viewer's childhood. The grandmother's faced warmth is a REGISTER shift for the viewer's-world beat — logged here as deliberate, the one plate in the episode that breaks the blank-oval anchor, because L9 is the one line set in the viewer's world rather than the deep past.
records.why: The tool's survival is proven by a face the viewer recognises from their own life, not by another prehistoric figure.
records.change: If Hadi judges the register shift a consistency break rather than a turn, L9 falls back to the grandmother plate + label and this record is amended.

records.element: Scene plate — dawn finale (L8, L10 + end card, reused)
records.choice: The series' Observations finale dawn plate, reused as in Ep.2/Ep.3: the song 'riding through them all' is declared over the bookend world, and the notes drift above it.
records.alternatives: A new dawn — rejected: bookend sameness across episodes is the device (series Chekhov).
records.context: N-08; format v4 end card rides the same plate.
records.why: The fourth archive joins the shelf in the same morning light as the others.
records.change: If the finale plate is ever rebuilt, every episode using it follows.

records.element: Element — the musical notes component (separate glyph elements)
records.choice: Five separate glyph components (♪♫♪♩♪, DejaVu Bold subset) in one layer, each independently positioned by the timeline function: ABSENT on L3 (plain words), standing IN A LINE on L4 and L7 (the beat holding words in order), TRAILING down the road on L6 (mouth to mouth, camp to camp), DRIFTING (three glyphs) over the dawn on L8. Hoverable as a layer, with its own note.
records.alternatives: Notes baked into generated plates (rejected — they must ARRANGE, and arrangement over time is a component's job, H-01); animated drawn notes (rejected — V-13 code-drawn figures; a typeset glyph is lettering, the series' own material).
records.context: H-01 separate components; S-08 motion must construct meaning — here the arrangement IS the mechanism, drawn.
records.why: The episode claims rhythm is an error-checking structure; the notes show structure appearing, travelling, and surviving — the claim performed, not decorated.
records.change: If the glyphs read as emoji-like clutter at phone size in QC frames, the set reduces to three and this record is amended.

records.element: Word placement — pale-sky scenes (grandmother, road, waterhole, childletters)
records.choice: Dark brown words, rust key word, no shadow, bands y 600–725 in each scene's pale sky — the Ep.2 waterhole/finale grammar.
records.alternatives: Cream words (invisible on these skies — the Ep.2 lesson, measured there).
records.context: V-16/V-14; contrast is the readability rule.
records.why: The words join each scene's own lettering system instead of importing the cave's.

records.choice: Cream words, amber key, text shadow, bands y 615/725 over the dusk sky — the episode's one dark scene gets the dark-scene grammar.
records.alternatives: Brown words (illegible against the dusk gradient's lower half).
records.why: The villain's beat still has to be readable; the palette shift also marks the fall from the day scenes.

records.choice: Dark brown words, rust key, bands y 815/935 — identical to Ep.2/Ep.3's finale grammar.
records.alternatives: None — bookend sameness is the point.
records.context: Series consistency (K-02) for the shared plate.

records.choice: faster-whisper word timestamps mapped to the script's exact words (165 display words); phrases of ≤3 words, cumulative, clearing before the next phrase; key words from the accent set at +18% with an overshoot pop.
records.alternatives: Whole-line captions (banned); karaoke over a full line (reads as a subtitle).
records.context: Format v4 word-animation spec; alignment log (3 repairs — two numeral hearings, one 'Plane' for 'Plain', timings kept) ships in the build folder.
records.why: At most 3 words exist at any instant, each arriving with its spoken moment.
records.change: Whisper boundary error >~150 ms on a re-alignment reopens the mapping.

records.choice: Guide-voice lines (same TTS voice as the series) normalised per line (A-11); a WARM synth-pad bed in Ep.2's chord family (a brighter register than Ep.3's cave bed — the pair of episodes deliberately differ, logged in both records) ducked ≈13 dB; stereo pan before mastering; master chain without dynaudnorm (standing law) to −14.00 LUFS / TP −1.88 on the delivered master. Music-only twin built alongside. No literal melody is composed for the song episode: the narration's own rhythm carries 'song'; a composed tune under narration would compete with the words (Q-e) — the notes component carries the music visually instead.
records.alternatives: A sung/hummed melodic bed — rejected for the Q-e reason above and because a recognisable tune would become a series signature by accident.
records.context: QC A-section; A-07 independent re-measurement in QC.
records.why: The bed warms; it never performs.
records.change: The cloned-voice pass swaps narration via the music-only twin.

records.choice: "A Song Remembers What Words Forget" — the episode's essence, unchanged from the draft (script DR-E4-CLICK).
records.alternatives: 'The First Memory Tool' (priority claim + spoils L7); 'Singing Directions' (a topic, not a gap).
records.context: S-09; the title is a small impossibility the piece resolves.
records.why: Songs are entertainment; remembering is for minds and books — the tap resolves which side is wrong.
records.change: CTR data after publish is the baseline.

records.choice: The opening-card frame (the grandmother singing the road, EARTH ONE + title), legible at 180 px; the script's cover line 'A SONG IS A MAP' is carried by the L2 in-scene label, the piece's own first reveal promoted into the scene (DR-E4-CLICK).
records.alternatives: The empty-road frame — rejected as cover: no person, no song; the paradox needs the singer.
records.why: A singer, two landmarks, and the title — the whole promise in one feed-sized frame.

records.choice: Grandmother plate + EARTH ONE + the episode title in rust/brown (the pale-sky grammar — amber title text would wash out on this sky; the colour change is this card's logged adaptation).
records.alternatives: Amber title text as on Ep.2/Ep.3's dark cards — rejected on measured legibility grounds (pale sky).
records.context: Format v4 container; cards are titles, not subtitles.
records.why: Same container, scene-matched ink — the container is recognised by structure, not by one colour.
records.change: If Hadi prefers strict colour sameness over legibility, the card darkens the plate instead — his call, flagged in the build report.

records.choice: Finale plate + 'FOLLOW FOR THE REST OF THE STORY' + NEXT tease 'MORE OF THE PLANET'S STORY' + EARTH ONE. No invented episode title: Ep.5 is not scripted, so the tease promises the series, not a fabricated next chapter.
records.alternatives: Inventing an Ep.5 title for symmetry with Ep.3's card — rejected on truth (T-18's spirit: packaging may not promise what doesn't exist).
records.context: Format v4 close: spoken bridge (L10) + FOLLOW end card.
records.why: The ask is made three ways — spoken bridge, card text, description.
records.change: When Ep.5 is scripted, a future iteration of this card names it.

records.choice: Small bold 'EARTH ONE' at top-left (x=100, y=265) during content, with the ink matched per scene: brown at 75% on the pale-sky scenes, cream at 69% on the dusk scene. DEVIATION from Ep.2/Ep.3's fixed cream bug — made because on Ep.4's pale skies the cream bug is effectively invisible (the known minor logged in Ep.2's DR-CARD-3, where a dark-bug variant was deferred as Hadi's call); for a new build the legible choice is taken and flagged for his verdict in the build report, not smuggled.
records.alternatives: Fixed cream (invisible here = attribution fails its only job); no bug (attribution lost entirely).
records.context: Format v4 container; V-14 safe rect; Ep.2 DR-CARD-3's deferred question, answered provisionally for pale scenes.
records.why: A bug that cannot be read is not a bug; per-scene ink keeps the attribution's job done in both palettes.
records.change: Hadi's verdict on this deviation settles it series-wide.

accepted_exceptions_note: No per-piece entry rides with this piece: the exceptions ledger was read directly at this migration (files/department-doc-anti-randomness.md §5, entries #1–#11) and no entry names eo-ep4 / Ep.4. One class-level ledger entry touches this piece's delivered state and is cited as class context where it belongs — NOT instantiated as a per-piece acceptance: ledger #7 (guide voice counts as final-for-now — Hadi's sprint framing; its timing superseded by the 2026-10-26 voice-upgrade mandate) in audio/audio.json. Ledger #8 (fastlane finals are mono against the P-04 stereo standard) was checked and does NOT apply: this piece's delivered audio is stereo (2 channels, ffprobe at this migration). Two Ep.4 items that might be mistaken for exceptions are neither: the L1 scrim defect (DR-TB-EP4-1-Z — scrims painted over the words in the first v4 render) was FIXED and frame-verified, not accepted (board cycle n=4); and the opening-card ink taken provisionally at build is not an acceptance — it is Hadi's open verdict, board Action #33 (metadata field cover_ink_verdict). Acceptances are revisable in this format (status_note practice); this piece has none to revise.
